notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 75 because none of my research tools worked this session. You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point, so I've left the notes out rather than write them from memory.

**What went wrong:**
- My first try to fetch six sources at once was refused because I had run out of tool calls for that turn. Those pages were Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill, the Pulpit Commentary and Spurgeon on biblehub.com, plus Augustine on newadvent.org.
- After that, every web fetch and web search timed out after 90 seconds. Even a simple `print(1)` timed out, so the problem is with the tool itself, not with any one website.
- The basic command-line tool still works, but it has no internet access, so it can't get the sources.

**What I'd read on the next try:**
- **Traditional verse-by-verse reading:** enduringword.com (Psalm 75); Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on biblehub.com; preceptaustin.org.
- **Differences between traditions:** wesley.nnu.edu (Wesley's notes), ligonier.org and thegospelcoalition.org for Reformed views, and the Lutheran sites. Likely topics are God "bearing up the pillars" of the earth (v. 3), "exaltation" coming from God alone (vv. 6–7), and the cup of wrath (v. 8).
- **Other views:** netbible.org's translator notes, such as who is speaking in vv. 2–5 and 10 and the meanings of "horn" and "outstretched neck." Also Augustine's *Exposition on the Psalms* on newadvent.org, which numbers this psalm 74. I'd also search for any modern teaching that uses v. 6 ("promotion comes not from the east…") to back up prosperity promises.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll start with those sources and write the notes verse by verse with a URL for each point.
